sources.title: Historical profile: birth, education, legal career, cabinet offices and elections
sources.findings: Read GNA historical October 2020 profile: March 29, 1944 Accra birth; father Edward held ceremonial presidency 1970–1972; University of Ghana economics 1964–1967, bachelor degree; English bar 1971, Ghanaian bar 1975, Coudert Brothers and Accra practice, 1979 firm, NPP 1992, three parliamentary elections, justice/attorney-general 2001, foreign minister 2003, government exit 2007, 2008/2012 presidential defeats and 2016 victory/2017 inauguration. Its 1996–2007 MP range conflicts with other accounts and conflates election/service; no exact parliamentary tenure adopted. Praise of personal peace-making, court automation or human-rights success is not independently audited. Criminal-libel repeal role reported here, no exhaustive legislative/docket audit claimed.

sources.publisher: University of Ghana Alumni Relations Office
sources.title: Alumni profile explicitly credited to Wikipedia; historical cross-reference only
sources.findings: Read University of Ghana alumni page, which explicitly credits Wikipedia. Supports 1967 BSc(Econ) wording but is not independent primary academic evidence. Historical current-president wording is stale. Oxford unfinished attendance and Inner/Middle Temple distinctions not used to invent an Oxford qualification or formal law degree. Birth/education cross-checked with GNA; no original diploma authenticated.

sources.publisher: UN Global Compact — Global Africa Business Initiative
sources.title: Historical participant biography: cabinet service, elections and 2021 inauguration
sources.findings: Read UN Global Compact GABI participant biography: three MP terms, attorney-general/justice minister 2001–2003, foreign minister April 2003–July 2007, 2008 runoff defeat, 2012 defeat and subsequent acceptance of court result, 2016 victory, December 7, 2020 re-election and January 7, 2021 inauguration. Current-president heading is historical despite 2026 website footer. Use year-level cabinet dates, avoid unsupported exact appointment day. MP wording 1997–2008 not silently merged with GNA conflicting range. No detailed five-to-four judgment interpretation or electoral vote-total arithmetic asserted.

sources.publisher: Permanent Mission of Ghana to the United Nations
sources.title: Second inauguration, 7 January 2021, with first inauguration and term context
sources.findings: Read Ghana UN Mission report of January 7, 2021 second and final inauguration, Bawumia continuing vice-president, December 7, 2020 election and January 7, 2017 first inauguration. Page uses both January 6 and January 7, 2025 endpoint language; dossier describes independently documented January 7 handover without asserting exact constitutional midnight. Published vote totals not used because unnecessary and not separately reconciled.

sources.title: Mahama sworn in after Akufo-Addo completes two terms, 7 January 2025
sources.findings: Read Reuters January 7, 2025 handover account: Mahama actually sworn in after December 2024 election, Akufo-Addo leaves after two terms. Separates current successor from predecessor and past 2017 transfer. Economic challenges provide context, not automatic personal criminal responsibility. Current sidebar/sidebar dates not treated as article updates; only relevant handover facts used.

sources.title: 2018 Citizens’ Budget: Free SHS implementation and One District One Factory launch
sources.findings: Read relevant education and industry sections of Finance Ministry 2018 Citizens’ Budget: Free SHS began September 2017 for first-year students, later-cohort expansion planned; One District One Factory launched August 25, 2017, proposal viability review and selection. Proposed factories/jobs, planned 2018 spending and claimed 2017 outputs are distinct. Do not assert every district achieved operational factory or treat forecast employment as realised. Later PDF hosting/crawl date not budget year; no exhaustive line-by-line budget or independent financial audit claimed.

sources.title: 2025 case study of Free SHS delivery, based on ministerial and team interviews
sources.findings: Read 2025 Harvard Ministerial Leadership case-study introduction and implementation sections: policy mandated by Akufo-Addo, delivered through Education Minister Prempeh and team, September 2017 rollout, eligible secondary pupils, fee/support scope and infrastructure/quality constraints. Case study based on interviews with programme participants, not independent experimental proof of all reported impacts. It explicitly does not represent institutional endorsement of conclusions. No universal elimination of inequality or independently verified enrolment effect size asserted.

sources.title: Board approval of Ghana ECF arrangement and initial disbursement, 17 May 2023
sources.findings: Read IMF-hosted May 17, 2023 approval content as rendered structured text: initial 36-month ECF, SDR 2.242 billion/about US$3 billion, immediate availability SDR 451.4 million/about US$600 million; macro stability/debt sustainability and restructuring. External shocks exacerbated pre-existing fiscal/debt weaknesses; no single-cause claim. Approval is not full disbursement or completed crisis recovery. Later extension/reviews are separate, so initial duration not asserted as unchanged current programme duration.

sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.title: September 2020 announcement of election to chair the Authority
sources.findings: Read ECOWAS official announcement: elected by 57th Authority summit, replacing Niger’s Mahamadou Issoufou. Body dateline September 9 and page September 10 are release dates, not substituted for actual election date September 7 confirmed contemporaneously by GBC. Authority chair is not Commission president.

sources.title: Contemporaneous report confirming ECOWAS election on 7 September 2020
sources.findings: Read GBC September 7, 2020 report and embedded Ministry of Information announcement text confirming election that Monday at Niamey summit. Did not play linked acceptance audio or claim independent inspection of original social-media account. Distinguishes election date from ECOWAS later release and predecessor Issoufou from successor Embaló.

sources.title: 7 July 2022 statement confirms Embaló succeeded Akufo-Addo at 3 July summit
sources.findings: Read MFWA July 7, 2022 statement: Embaló elected July 3 at 61st summit, succeeds Akufo-Addo after two terms, regional coups/security challenges remain. Unrelated sentence incorrectly sequences Embaló February 2020 inauguration after a December 2021 election; do not adopt that chronology. Positive endorsement is advocacy, not independent outcome evaluation. July 3 succession is corroborated by GNA search preview and contemporaneous draft communiqué context, not a claim those full final primary proceedings were inspected.

sources.title: Completed meeting between current and former presidents in Nima, 17 November 2026
sources.findings: Read MyJoyOnline November 17, 2026 completed-meeting report: incumbent Mahama visits former president at Nima residence with Julius Debrah and Stan Xoese Dogbe; national/international matters discussed. No specific agreement, new post, return to presidency or motive inferred. Actual article text supports life/activity status; image markers are not visual identity review.
